name: AdaPlanner: Adaptive Planning from Feedback with Language Models
venue: NeurIPS 2023 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36); preprint arXiv:2305.16653 (cs.CL)
authors_affiliation: Haotian Sun, Yuchen Zhuang, Lingkai Kong, Bo Dai, Chao Zhang. All from Georgia Institute of Technology (Sun and Zhuang contributed equally).
task_domain: LLM-agent sequential decision-making / planning in interactive grounded environments (embodied text-game ALFWorld and web-interaction MiniWoB++).
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, closed-loop sequential decision-making. An LLM agent is given a task goal, a list of admissible actions, and (optionally) a small number of expert demonstrations, then must generate and execute a plan in an environment that returns natural-language observations. The setting is online/test-time: the agent acts, observes feedback, and adaptively revises its plan within an episode. Supervision is limited to a few human demonstrations (or none), with no gradient training of the LLM; environment feedback (observations and assertion checks) supplies the refinement signal. Evaluated on ALFWorld (embodied household tasks) and MiniWoB++ (web GUI tasks).
what_is_retrieved: Successful plans/skills (full code-style solution() programs together with their environment interactions) stored as few-shot exemplars; at plan time these discovered skills plus human-written demonstrations are injected into the prompt.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID: a static set of human-written task demonstrations plus a GROWING episodic skill memory that the agent writes during deployment via skill discovery (successful trajectories archived after a filtering step).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Neither a learned ranking nor a completeness objective; relevant skill(s)/demonstration(s) are selected by task resemblance/task type and supplied as few-shot exemplars. Selection is small fixed-set rather than top-k ranked retrieval. [uncertain]
retrieval_unit: skill-or-program: a full code-based plan (a Pythonic solution() function) representing a successful trajectory for a task, plus the corresponding human demonstrations; effectively a full-trajectory/case unit expressed as executable code.
index_source: Hybrid: offline human-written demonstrations (one example per task) combined with an online/test-time-induced skill memory grown via the trial-and-error skill discovery loop during deployment.
index_structure_topology: Skill memory keyed by task / task-type resemblance (similar tasks reuse stored skills); no learned vector index or graph is described. Effectively a metadata/task-keyed flat store. [uncertain]
retriever_type: No learned/dense retriever; skill/demonstration selection is by task resemblance (task-type matching) and supplied as in-context exemplars. Closest to a rule/metadata-keyed selection rather than BM25 or dense retrieval. [uncertain]
retriever_learning_signal: none (no trained retriever). Which skill is retained is decided by a downstream-task-effectiveness filter (skill filtering: keep the discovered skill only if it improves success rate), but skill selection at plan time is not a learned retrieval policy.
query_construction: The query/key is the current task goal plus the list of admissible actions (and current state for refinement); resembling tasks trigger reuse of stored skills as exemplars. Raw task description is used; no synthetic query expansion.
query_granularity: task-level (skills/demonstrations are selected once at initial plan generation, t=0, conditioned on the task goal). Refinement operates at sub-goal/step level but the skill retrieval itself is task-level.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot for skill/demonstration retrieval (assembled into the prompt at initial planning). Plan refinement is iterative/active but it re-prompts the same exemplars rather than retrieving new ones.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Skill/demonstration injection is on a fixed schedule at plan generation. The separate plan-refinement trigger is an assertion-failure / out-of-plan signal: each sub-goal ends with an assertion checked at N checkpoints; assertion failure (misaligned observation vs prediction) triggers out-of-plan refinement, while aligned feedback triggers in-plan refinement via ask_LLM().
reranking: None. No reranking stage over retrieved skills/demonstrations.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at retrieval time. (A skill-filtering step occurs at write/storage time, discarding skills that do not boost success rate, but retrieved exemplars are injected verbatim into the prompt without post-retrieval reranking, compression, or distillation.)
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation / skill reuse: discovered skills and human demonstrations are placed into the code-style LLM prompt as few-shot exemplars to ground initial plan generation and refinement.
planning_integration: one-shot exemplars at plan time combined with a closed-loop plan-then-refine loop: AdaPlanner first generates a complete code-based plan (decomposed into sub-goals with assertions), executes it, and applies in-plan refinement (ask_LLM extracts info, integrated into current plan) or out-of-plan refinement (regenerate/revise the whole plan via refine-then-resume from a saved breakpoint). Retrieved skills serve as initial-plan exemplars.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-sub-goal / per-checkpoint: refinement is woven in at N sub-goal assertion checkpoints within a rollout (in-plan refinement is a one-step ask_LLM action; out-of-plan refinement revises the whole plan at a checkpoint). Skill retrieval itself is per-answer (per-episode, at plan time).
retrieved_item_representation: executable program / skill: the injected item is a Pythonic code-based solution() function (a successful plan plus interactions), used as a free-text/code exemplar in the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: procedural skill / reusable code plan derived from a successful full trajectory (a code-style plan that decomposes the task into sub-goals); above raw trajectory, framed as a reusable skill exemplar.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Code-style (Pythonic) prompting constrains the LLM generation space to mitigate hallucination; assertion-based self-checking detects misaligned (out-of-plan) feedback and triggers correction; skill filtering discards non-generalizing skills before they enter memory, guarding against episode-specific noise.
memory_type: skill-library (skill memory module archiving successful code-based plans/trajectories as reusable few-shot skills).
write_back: Yes. Successful plans discovered during deployment are written into the skill memory (after a filtering check) and reused as few-shot exemplars for resembling tasks.
online_growth: Yes. The skill memory grows at test time via skill discovery; e.g., in MiniWoB++ AdaPlanner starts with 38 human demonstrations and automatically discovers 21 additional skill examples, yielding 59 examples for 53 tasks.
write_back_trigger: on-success only, gated by an effectiveness filter: a candidate skill is created when AdaPlanner successfully completes a task (skill acquisition); it is retained (written to memory) only if including it improves success rate during skill filtering, otherwise discarded.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only for memory: only successful plans are archived as skills (failed trajectories are not stored as reusable skills). Within an episode, failed assertions/out-of-plan feedback drive immediate plan revision but are not persisted as negative cases. Contrasts with Reflexion, which stores past-failure reflections.
memory_evolution_update: append-only with a filtering gate (discovered skills are appended if they improve success rate, discarded otherwise); no described merge/delta-update/refine-overwrite of already-stored skills.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Skill/demonstration selection is not an RL- or value-optimized retrieval policy; it is task-resemblance-based reuse. The only optimization is a success-rate filter at storage time.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private skill memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework experience sharing.
benchmarks: ALFWorld (134 tasks across 6 task types: Pick, Clean, Heat, Cool, Examine, Pick two) and MiniWoB++ (53 tasks: 9 with feedback, 44 without feedback).
baselines: ALFWorld: BUTLER (training-based), ReAct, Reflexion (implicit closed-loop). MiniWoB++: CC-Net and WGE (training-based), WebN-T5-3B (finetuning-based), RCI (implicit closed-loop). DEPS is discussed as a related strict closed-loop method. Backends: GPT-3 (text-davinci-002), GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo / text-davinci-003).
key_metrics: Success rate (%); sample efficiency measured as number of expert demonstrations/samples used.
headline_result: AdaPlanner outperforms SOTA baselines by 3.73% on ALFWorld and 4.11% on MiniWoB++ while using 2x and 600x fewer samples respectively; overall success rate 91.79% on ALFWorld (GPT-3) and 91.11% on MiniWoB++ tasks with feedback (92.87% over all 53 MiniWoB++ tasks).
ablations: (1) Number of closed-loop refinements: success rate rises monotonically with each refinement and AdaPlanner beats Reflexion at every iteration, even with as few as 2 total demonstrations across six tasks. (2) Code interface ablation: removing the code interface (natural-language plans) drops ALFWorld from 81% to 46% and MiniWoB++ from 93% to 66%. (3) Skill discovery ablation: with vs without skill discovery; success rate nearly doubles on ALFWorld and rises ~15% on MiniWoB++. (4) GPT-3 vs GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo) showing AdaPlanner's resilience to hallucination via code prompts.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task success rates are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG/completeness) are reported separately (retrieval here is skill reuse, not ranked retrieval).
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (task success rate). Process-level insight is given indirectly via success rate vs number of closed-loop refinements (showing intermediate refinement quality) and sample-efficiency curves, but no formal step-wise/faithfulness metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Strong efficiency focus: 2x fewer samples on ALFWorld, ~600x fewer samples on MiniWoB++ vs CC-Net; the refine-then-resume mechanism resumes from a saved breakpoint instead of restarting episodes, reducing the number of LLM/API calls; assertions are checked only at N crucial sub-goal checkpoints to cut API-call count. gpt-3.5-turbo noted as ~10x cheaper than text-davinci-002/003 but with more hallucination.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed, small exemplar count: ALFWorld uses one demonstration per task (6 total, half of what ReAct/Reflexion use); MiniWoB++ uses 38 human demos + 21 discovered skills (59 examples for 53 tasks). Selection count is fixed/budget-capped per task rather than adaptive top-k.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (reuse skills for resembling tasks), Reuse (skills as few-shot exemplars), Revise (in-plan/out-of-plan plan refinement from feedback), Retain (skill discovery archives successful plans after filtering). 4-flag: [Retrieve: yes (lightweight, task-resemblance), Reuse: yes, Revise: yes, Retain: yes]. Note: the work does not frame itself as CBR.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not explicitly frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it realizes CBR-like mechanisms (skill reuse + revise + retain) under the terms skill discovery and closed-loop plan refinement.
index_content_separation: N/A (skills stored as full code plans; no separate lightweight index vs heavy content described).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; environment interaction via ALFWorld/MiniWoB++ action APIs and a code-execution interface, not a tool index/MCP).
adaptation_mechanism: execution-feedback-driven revision: a reused skill/plan is adapted via in-plan refinement (ask_LLM extracts info integrated into the plan) and out-of-plan refinement (LLM regenerates/revises the whole plan from an assertion-failure feedback message, then refine-then-resume from a saved breakpoint). Not verbatim ICL only; the plan is actively revised.
builds_on: ReAct (action grounding from feedback), Reflexion (self-revision from trials), RCI (plan-then-act), code-as-prompt / program-of-thought ideas (e.g., code-generation prompting reduces ambiguity), Chain-of-Thought and Zero-Shot Planner as earlier open-loop LLM planners; ALFWorld and MiniWoB++ as environments.
contrasts_with: Open-loop planners (Chain-of-Thought, Zero-Shot Planner, HuggingGPT, Chameleon); implicit closed-loop methods that fix the initial plan and only adjust the current action (ReAct, Inner Monologue, Reflexion, RCI); and DEPS, which needs a trained plan selector and task-specific data; AdaPlanner instead refines the whole plan purely via LLM prompting.
lineage: Group C (RAG planning): LLM planners that adaptively refine plans from environment feedback and reuse self-discovered skills, in the lineage of feedback-driven closed-loop LLM agents (ReAct -> Reflexion -> AdaPlanner) with an experience/skill-memory (growing episodic store) component.
